oracle_provenance.method: structured hex mesh over the stated stack, solved twice; steady conduction with orthotropic laminate and film boundaries. The reported quantity is the difference between the two solves.
oracle_provenance.reference_grid: 1.0 mm in-plane, 16 elements through the stack
oracle_provenance.repro_method: both configurations at 1.0, 0.7 and 1.4 mm in-plane grids
oracle_provenance.pass_tol_basis: 5% of the delta, which binds: 2x the measured grid spread is 0.234 K, well inside it. The HBM deltas were measured too and are NOT scored -- their grid spread (4.35% and 7.24%) exceeds the absolutes they are built from, so their bands would have to be 8.7% and 14.5% of the quantity, which is a band widened until a right and a wrong answer both score (#487)
oracle_provenance.gt_type_note: The reference is what a competently-driven conduction solve of this stated package predicts for the change. The package is synthetic; there is no measurement of it and none is claimed.

delta_t_asic_c.description: Change in the logic die's peak steady temperature when the TIM is upgraded from 118 um / 4.7 W/m/K to 32 um / 8.4 W/m/K at an unchanged load. Negative: the better TIM cools it.
delta_t_asic_c.gt_value_source: THIS REPO'S OWN ORACLE, AND NOTHING EXTERNAL CHECKS THE SETUP THAT PRODUCED IT. gt_value is the difference between what solution/pkg25d.py computes for the two configurations on the 1.0 mm reference grid: modified (TIM 32 um, k 8.4) minus baseline (TIM 118 um, k 4.7), with the load and both film coefficients identical. The package is synthetic (source_type = novel_variant), so no published source reports a value for it and moving the operating point cannot produce one. What makes this a RELATION rather than a second absolute is that the two runs share every input except the TIM -- and the measured spread below shows how far that falls short of cancelling: the delta's grid spread is 0.43%, against 0.36% for the absolute it is built from, so the cancellation a relation is supposed to buy is worth almost nothing here. It is NOT free, and the reason is the constraint recorded on #487: a relation cancels common mode only when the two runs share the thing that varies, and a TIM thickness change moves the through-thickness element distribution. The KPI survives on the other property instead -- a pair_delta sits 20 band widths from its null answer, and a 1-D resistance estimate of it spans -4.3 K to -75.4 K depending on the spreading area assumed, the closest being 25% low.
